groups.reference_problem: HEAD VARIATION (IDLE): eye-like paired lights, changing void width/tilt, unknown attachment.
groups.why_it_fails: Face cues defeat the faceless brief; separate studies cannot establish continuity.
groups.research_principle: Primary construction remains stable beneath secondary variation.
groups.production_rule: Build one registered void/root system; vary unequal tips around it. Remove eyes/skull pips. Body-hidden tests cannot substitute for body-only tests.

groups.reference_problem: HEAD DURING ACTION: missile-like leading void, no root or returning shape.
groups.why_it_fails: Shape change lacks a causal origin and recovery.
groups.research_principle: A smear must connect to its preceding anatomical source.
groups.production_rule: Keep neck/root attachment, deform along the actual body motion, then recover a recognizable void. A stretched head cannot read as a launched projectile.

groups.reference_problem: IDLE: final frontal turn mixed with breathing; neck/limb continuity unclear.
groups.why_it_fails: An orientation change masquerades as a loop; quiet body remains interchangeable.
groups.research_principle: Gesture and unequal overlap convey intent more clearly than a contour bob.
groups.production_rule: Keep one facing, support and grip ownership through the loop; use unequal body rhythms derived from the eventual law, not a whole-sprite bob.

groups.reference_problem: WALK: repeated wide splits; missing passing/opposite support; reads as slow run.
groups.why_it_fails: No complete weight-transfer cycle is visible.
groups.research_principle: Locomotion must show distinct phases and alternating support.
groups.production_rule: Author contact, low, passing and opposite contact for the actual locomotion cycle. Do not add a walk input or new walk speed because the reference has a row.

groups.reference_problem: RUN: athletic lunge repetition, ambiguous paired limbs, hand/shirt changes, unproven seam.
groups.why_it_fails: A heroic wedge and incoherent ownership conceal the person's movement.
groups.research_principle: Arm participation and torso motion are coupled; contact phases must remain identifiable.
groups.production_rule: Track both legs and anatomical arms through a complete cycle. Couple arm restriction to torso compensation. Preserve clothes and grip; check three loops and both facings.

groups.reference_problem: JUMP: no launch coil; overlapping limbs; compressed ending; board positions are not a trajectory.
groups.why_it_fails: Intent and release cannot be distinguished from a tuck or kick.
groups.research_principle: Connected torso construction and purposeful spacing distinguish release from a folded pose.
groups.production_rule: Show release immediately after real launch, optional compact rising pose, apex adjustment and descent transition. Fit visual compression around existing movement, never before input takes effect.

groups.reference_problem: FALL: grounded first pose, seated/kick-like forward feet, unclear descent and restoration.
groups.why_it_fails: A passive loss of support reads as another commanded action.
groups.research_principle: Gesture identifies intention; an unexpected loss of support is not the same action as a jump.
groups.production_rule: Separate falling from rising using unsupported pelvis, preparation for landing and non-kicking feet. A ledge fall must work without any jump anticipation.

groups.reference_problem: DASH: fixed lunge, giant final head, no exit/reconnection.
groups.why_it_fails: Head spectacle replaces state change and body consequence.
groups.research_principle: Visual direction and transition must communicate the core mechanic.
groups.production_rule: Give body distinct entry, transit and exit shapes within 150 ms; use directionally attached deformation. Exit reconnects to the true grounded/air/attack state.

groups.reference_problem: ATTACK 1: repeated guards, changing striker, lifted foot/arm detour, no source return.
groups.why_it_fails: The strike lacks one cause, contact and consequence.
groups.research_principle: Strong keys and a readable return must fit responsive action timing.
groups.production_rule: Use one consistent anatomical striker/grip; compact startup, forward contact, distinct whiff/confirmed recovery. Keep a supported foot and a readable return.

groups.reference_problem: ATTACK 2: flame as weapon, giant smear with small body change, unstable return; no heavy action in game.
groups.why_it_fails: It promises mechanics and reach that do not exist.
groups.research_principle: The actual mechanic and context determine the visual promise.
groups.production_rule: Do not produce a heavy state. Reuse only the abstract compression/contact/recovery lesson in existing armed/finisher confirmation, without larger reach or fire damage.

groups.reference_problem: ATTACK 3: absent upward mechanic, changing strike direction, arm/flame ambiguity, spell arc.
groups.why_it_fails: An unsupported move and magical ownership obscure actual direction.
groups.research_principle: Action cues must identify the mechanic and direction the player actually controls.
groups.production_rule: Do not produce an up-attack state. Every existing attack must clearly face and contact in its actual direction, with attached body and weapon.

groups.reference_problem: HURT: attack-like guards, unspecified impact direction, no restored support, torso/limb drift.
groups.why_it_fails: A voluntary attack and involuntary flinch become indistinguishable.
groups.research_principle: Unexpected postural disturbance and support restoration differ from deliberate action.
groups.production_rule: Show unexpected contraction/support disturbance followed by restoration within the hurt visual window. Use directional response only if existing data provides direction.

groups.reference_problem: DEATH: merged legs, disappearing final body, unknown final contacts.
groups.why_it_fails: Collapse loses material mass and anatomical cause.
groups.research_principle: Solid connected masses must survive changing balance and contact.
groups.production_rule: Track loss of support into a settled body with both limbs accounted for. Keep physical body present; flame loses structure separately. Respect actual floor and reload clock.

groups.reference_problem: EXTRA: detached blobs/streak/U-curl, no event/root/endpoints, particle/aura association.
groups.why_it_fails: Decoration invents an emitter or projectile.
groups.research_principle: Secondary motion and smear require an attached cause and temporal endpoints.
groups.production_rule: No autonomous effect animation from these samples. A needed smear belongs to an existing event and named attached part, with readable source and destination.

groups.reference_problem: Large views: unregistered feet/stance, shifting head volume, jacket/hand uncertainty.
groups.why_it_fails: Inconsistent construction cannot be a production model sheet.
groups.research_principle: Stable construction and selective detail preserve identity through projection.
groups.production_rule: Derive a fresh native-size construction sheet, fixed landmarks and material masses. Track projected shortening rather than shrinking body dimensions per pose.

groups.reference_problem: SILHOUETTE: faint generic outline, flame included, no distinct pose exploration.
groups.why_it_fails: The head can conceal a body without identity.
groups.research_principle: Body shape, pose variety and gameplay-background readability must be established before polish.
groups.production_rule: Judge new body-only poses at actual gameplay size and compare transitions. Require the chosen later law to survive flame, texture and color removal.
